answer: Bind each agent identity to one hardware attestation from a secure enclave, verified once per device. A nebula of free keys then collapses to the count of real machines, because one chip signs exactly one identity and its attestation cannot be copied to another key. That chip is the bridge between a key and a physical device, since the attestation is issued for that hardware alone. An attacker chasing 1,000 fake agents must buy 1,000 devices at about $80 each, roughly $80,000 in hardware, while one honest operator needs just one device, its own knoll.
